card.summary: no service and no account; MIT-licensed client and server, packaged in the eduVPN server repository

free_tier.stated: no service and no account; MIT-licensed client and server, packaged in the eduVPN server repository

egress.terms: not applicable; the software states no volume; ingress: tcp

record.tooling: make install adds systemd units; DEB and RPM packages in the eduVPN repo
record.chaining: rides any HTTPS reverse proxy, so it composes with a host that already serves a website and with a CDN that passes an Upgrade header.
record.binding_note: the constraint is a server host, mitigated by the fact that it is designed to sit behind a reverse proxy on an existing HTTPS port

identity_cost.detail: no account for the tool; the eduVPN ecosystem around it issues accounts separately

record.reliability_note: client requires TLS 1.3 or newer; on Linux --fwmark may be needed to avoid a routing loop, and that flag needs root or CAP_NET_ADMIN
record.confidence_note: a measured run through an nginx or HAProxy front would raise it; eduVPN publishes deployment docs but no throughput figure

evidence.proved: "proxy UDP connections over HTTP(s). The main use case is to proxy WireGuard packets" and "This proxy thus needs to run for every client and for a server"
"This project started with a UDP to TCP approach, but later moved to HTTP for use behind a reverse proxy"
"The goal of this project is NOT to work around intentional state/organizational network blocks/censorship"

record.notes: Reverse proxy software wrapping WireGuard over TCP, maintained for eduVPN deployments. Shares port 443 with HTTPS web servers via HTTP Upgrade headers.

extras.wg_detail: client listens on 127.0.0.1:51821 and the WireGuard config sets Endpoint = 127.0.0.1:51821; server runs 'proxyguard-server --listen 0.0.0.0:51821 --to 127.0.0.1:51820'
extras.volume_stated: not applicable; the software states no volume
extras.transit_note: through the server half, which forwards to the local WireGuard port
extras.hosting_requirement: a server host with an HTTP listener, preferably behind a reverse proxy on 443; a user half runs on the device
